subject: Logo opt-in & embargo — clarify publicity/redline requests
messages:
From: Pauline Rivers <pauline.rivers@brightpath.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@brightpath.io>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Logo opt-in & embargo — initial redline request

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightPath is excited about the integration. Legal is asking for two small clarifications in the MSA/order form publicity language before we can sign:

1) We want an explicit opt-in for logo/reference usage (customer must provide affirmative consent after go-live). No implied grant at signature.
2) We need an embargo window — BrightPath asks that any public announcement using our name/logo not occur until we have approved messaging and a coordinated launch date (we propose up to 30 days post-consent).

I've attached our suggested redlines (BrightPath_Requested_Redlines.pdf) on the publicity clause and a short example clause for an opt-in flow. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept opt-in (vs. default permission), and whether the embargo language is workable? We also need to understand what assets you'll need and an expected turnaround.

Turnaround: ideally 3 business days for a quick redline, since we are targeting a pilot announcement window.

Thanks — Pauline
Pauline Rivers
Head of Partnerships, BrightPath
pauline.rivers@brightpath.io
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@brightpath.io>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logo opt-in & embargo — initial redline request

Ben / Marissa — looping you in.

Summary of asks from BrightPath: opt-in for logo/reference, 30-day embargo after consent, narrow publicity carveouts (no press release or case study without separate approval). Attached: my quick draft suggestion for a compromise clause (I can paste text if helpful).

Questions for legal/redlines:
- Can we accept opt-in (customer must provide a separate written consent after go-live) instead of an automatic perpetual license?
- Is an embargo tied to the customer-approved launch date (rather than signature) a workable risk profile?

Marissa — do we have the asset lockups and brand guidelines they need? They mentioned wanting to review a sample logo lockup. If we can confirm asset delivery timelines, we can include that in the mutual action plan.

I think this is a reasonable ask for a pilot account. Ben — your thoughts on commercial tradeoffs (discounts / marketing credit) if they choose to opt-in?

Naomi
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logo opt-in & embargo — initial redline request

Naomi — short note from sales POV.

I support opt-in. Buyers in this segment prefer control and offering opt-in gives us a better close rate. For tradeoffs, propose: if BrightPath opts into marketing (i.e., provides consent within 30 days of launch), we offer a co-marketing credit (10% credit against first invoice) or a feature spotlight in our partner page.

Embargo: 30 days post-consent is fine. Suggest we add language that allows Redwood to request an exception for joint press (subject to customer approval) so we don't lose momentum on product stories.

I will call Pauline later today to align on timeline and push for a rapid sign-off.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logo opt-in & embargo — assets and timing

Naomi / Ben — marketing can support this.

What BrightPath will need from us:
- Official logo lockup (SVG + PNG) and color usage guidance
- A short 1-paragraph partner blurb for citation
- Contact for press coordination

We can deliver the logo pack and blurb within 48 hours of receiving the consent language (or earlier if they sign off on our standard lockup). I attached the Press_Asset_Manifest.xlsx that lists the exact file formats we provide.

On embargo handling: we'd prefer the embargo window to be symmetric (i.e., neither party may announce until mutual launch readiness; but we can accept customer-first approval). Let's keep the contract language clear about the approval workflow.

Marissa Cole
Director, Marketing Programs
Redwood Inference

We've also added a clause requiring a 5-business-day review window for final messaging.
